activity.notes: Frederick Augustus III, Elector of Saxony, became the first King of Saxony as Frederick Augustus I on 20 December 1806 after Saxony's elevation to a kingdom in the Napoleonic settlement. He remained King of Saxony until his death on 5 May 1827. This identity must not be confused with the earlier Elector Frederick Augustus I, better known as Augustus II the Strong, King of Poland.

sources.title: Friedrich August I., der Gerechte
sources.citation_text: Neue Deutsche Biographie identifies Friedrich August as the first King of Saxony from 1806 and records his death on 5 May 1827, while describing the 1806 settlement that elevated Saxony to a kingdom.

sources.title: Friedrich August I, First King of Saxony
sources.citation_text: Staatliche Kunstsammlungen Dresden identifies Friedrich August I (1750-1827) as the first King of Saxony, supporting the royal identity used by ATLAS.
